title: How to use an inhaler
what: An inhaler delivers medicine straight to your lungs. The right technique is key. Otherwise the medicine stays in your mouth.
why: For asthma, COPD, and other airway conditions, as your doctor prescribes.
tell_doctor: Which inhalers you have and how often you use them
If you need your rescue inhaler more often than usual
Ask your doctor to check your technique at your visit

prepare.title: Type
prepare.text: There are spray inhalers and powder inhalers, and the technique is different. Read the leaflet for yours.

prepare.title: Medicine
prepare.text: Your doctor will tell you which inhaler is for every day and which is for attacks. Do not stop them on your own.

bring: Your inhalers, to your doctor's visit
Your spacer, if you have one
steps: Take off the cap. Shake a spray inhaler well
Sit or stand up straight and breathe out gently, away from the inhaler
Seal your lips tightly around the mouthpiece
Spray inhaler: press down and at the same time start a slow, deep breath in
Powder inhaler: take a quick, strong breath in
Hold your breath for 5 to 10 seconds, then breathe out gently
If you need a second puff, wait about a minute
After a steroid inhaler, rinse your mouth and spit
feel: A cool feeling or a taste in your mouth
Sometimes a scratchy throat or a cough
after: Watch the dose counter or expiry date
Keep the mouthpiece clean and dry
Always carry your rescue inhaler with you
red_flags: Your rescue inhaler does not help, it is hard to talk, or your lips turn blue: call emergency services

faq.a: After steroid inhalers, medicine left in the mouth can cause thrush and a hoarse voice.

faq.q: How do I know if my inhaler is empty?
faq.a: Check the dose counter. If there is none, count your puffs. Shaking the canister is not a reliable way to tell.

reminders.text: Time for your inhaler. Breathe out, breathe in slowly, hold your breath, and rinse your mouth after a steroid inhaler.
